title: Understanding Flatness in Generative Models: Its Role and Benefits
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
publication_status_observed: arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.11078v2 [cs.CV] 6 Aug 2025; submitted to IEEE ICCV per header
main_claims: Flat minima improve robustness against perturbations in the target prior distribution in diffusion models, provably bounding the divergence between learned and true distributions.
SAM induces significantly flatter loss surfaces in diffusion models than SWA, EMA, or Input Perturbation as measured by LPF and perturbation-based metrics.
Flat diffusion models (trained with SAM) exhibit reduced exposure bias and greatly improved robustness to 8-bit model quantization compared to baselines.
methodology: The authors derive theoretical bounds linking parameter-space flatness (delta-flat minima) to distributional gap robustness for score-based generative models. They then empirically train ADM diffusion models on CIFAR-10, LSUN Tower, and FFHQ using SAM, SWA, EMA, and Input Perturbation, evaluating FID, LPF flatness, exposure bias (L2 norm gap), and quantization degradation under 8-bit precision.
key_results: SAM+ADM achieves FID 9.01 vs. 34.47 for plain ADM on CIFAR-10 at 20 sampling steps, the largest improvement among all flatness methods.
LPF flatness for ADM+SAM is 0.063 vs. 0.097 for ADM, 0.099 for ADM+SWA, and 0.099 for ADM+EMA, showing SAM exclusively reduces flatness.
Under 8-bit quantization, ADM+SAM FID degrades by only -0.07 (20 steps) vs. +13.65 for plain ADM, demonstrating near-zero quantization sensitivity.
limitations: Theoretical analysis uses a simplified random feature model for the score network, which may not fully represent large-scale diffusion architectures.
Experiments are on relatively low-resolution datasets (up to 64x64); extension to higher-resolution tasks is left to future work.
The paper focuses on diffusion models rather than discriminative classifiers, so its findings do not directly address SAM's OOD generalization in supervised settings.
relevance_to_rq: This paper empirically and theoretically compares SAM and SWA as flatness-oriented methods in a generative setting, finding SAM produces substantially flatter minima than SWA/EMA. This directly informs the RQ by showing that SAM and SWA differ in their realized flatness even when both nominally seek flat minima, a key confound the RQ intends to disentangle in discriminative OOD tasks.

key_quotes.text: we find that ensemble-like averaging, such as +SWA and +EMA, fail to induce additional flatness. In contrast, +SAM finds a flatter loss surface by explicitly perturbing model weights
key_quotes.context: Flatness measurement results showing SAM uniquely reduces LPF, while SWA and EMA do not
